paragraphs.source_en:
Cp. Ruins (end ch. 24): ‘. . . this further truth will then appear . . . That real objects have in them-
selves an identical, constant, and invariable mode of existence, and that in your organs exists a similar
mode of being affected and impressed by them. But at the same time, inasmuch as these organs are
liable to the direction of your will, you may receive different impressions, and find yourselves under
different relations towards the same objects; so that you are with respect to them, as it were, a sort of
mirror, capable of reflecting them such as they are, and capable of disfiguring and misrepresenting
them.’
